clue.text: We'll 16 17, sort of 17's good luck today!

indicators.note: the answer to 16 is pinch, and to pinch here is to grip or hold, so the first word holds the blow

parts.note: the 'll is the future tense, leaving we
the answer to 17 is punch, and a punch is a hit
a rabbit punch is a sort of punch; the 's stays as a plain S

explanation.surface: A playground promise to pinch and punch someone, with luck wished for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: With 16 and 17 in, the clue reads 'We'll pinch punch': WE pinches (holds) HIT. British children say 'pinch, punch, first of the month', and 'white rabbits' said that morning is meant to bring luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the phrase first thing on the first day of a month is a British superstition believed to bring luck.

clue.text: Needing to be brief, Premiership players ring supervisors

definitions.meaning: a football club in the English top division, known in short form by its initials
a governing body that oversees professional boxing, whose fights take place in a ring

explanation.surface: Footballers needing to be quick about it surround the referees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needing to be brief' tells you to use the short form. West Bromwich Albion is an English football club; the World Boxing Association governs boxing matches.
explanation.definitionFit: The three initials abbreviate both West Bromwich Albion, a football team, and the World Boxing Association, which sanctions title fights.

clue.text: Aegean naval base is reportedly on edge, looking skyward

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is must be written as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: the word 'is' sounds like the letters I and Z run together

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking skyward means the letters run upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: an edge or border is a rim

explanation.surface: A naval base on the Aegean is said to be tense and watching the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On edge' suggests nervousness, but 'edge' gives RIM, reversed to MIR by 'looking skyward' because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Izmir is a Turkish port city on the Aegean coast that hosts a naval base.

clue.text: Coral's "shellfish stinger", trimmings of appetiser removed

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: removed says the letters of the appetiser are taken out of the stinging shellfish phrase

parts.note: a whelk is an edible sea snail, a shellfish
a hornet is a large stinging wasp
to whet the appetite is to stimulate it, so an appetiser is a whet

explanation.surface: A coral is described as a stinging shellfish, after the garnish has been trimmed from a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trimmings of appetiser removed' means the letters W, H, E, T of WHET are removed one by one, in order, from WHELKHORNET.
explanation.definitionFit: Elkhorn coral is a branching Caribbean reef coral named for its antler-like shape.

clue.text: Port broadcast first part of rescue …

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the airwaves, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: in the phrase air-sea rescue, the first part is air

explanation.surface: A harbour transmits the opening stage of a rescue mission.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue and 26-down share the phrase air-sea rescue; each part is heard as a place or a word. Ayr is a Scottish seaside town on the Firth of Clyde.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr is a harbour town on the west coast of Scotland, a port on the Firth of Clyde.

clue.text: Rudely kiss head and you might get off here

parts.note: buss is an old, rough word for a kiss
the head is the top of something

explanation.surface: Snog someone's head roughly and you may be told to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get off' hints at a romantic encounter, but it means leaving a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop on a bus route is a place where passengers leave the vehicle.

clue.text: One imposing stretch is clear about 17

indicators.note: about means turning round, so the words is and clear are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
clear as in clear profit, net of costs
the answer to 17 is a blow, and a oner is slang for a heavy single blow

explanation.surface: Someone stretching a point is clear about a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses IS + NET to give TENSI; then a oner, slang for a heavy punch (the 17 answer), completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tensioner is a device that applies tension, keeping a belt or chain taut.

clue.text: Plump lady of the night wants to employ Iron Age dwelling

parts.note: plump and round both mean chubby
ho is slang for a prostitute, a lady of the night
to employ is to use

explanation.surface: A chubby streetwalker needs to make use of a prehistoric home.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron Age Britons lived in circular thatched huts that archaeologists name after their shape.

clue.text: One's top and cap removed, tourist gives hand on farm

indicators.note: removed says the first letter and the cap are taken out of the tourist

parts.note: a holidaymaker is a tourist

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, here of One's

parts.note: a cap or covering on a pot is a lid

explanation.surface: A tourist has lost hat and top and ends up helping on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking O (One's top) and LID (cap) from HOLIDAYMAKER leaves the answer. It is also a wild swinging punch, fitting the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmhand who cuts and dries grass for fodder in summer does this job.

clue.text: The first one is unfortunately right

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters of one is are muddled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gloomy remark that the leader happened to be correct.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder of two people sharing a name, or the top in rank, is the first.

clue.text: Half-inch cut, not entirely clean, to the head

indicators.note: to the head says the shortened word goes at the front
not entirely means the last letter is dropped from the word for clean

parts.note: clean means pure
a loin is a cut of meat

explanation.surface: Instructions for a short haircut, not fully tidy, at the top of the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-inch' is Cockney rhyming slang for pinch, meaning steal: a British usage. PUR (pure 'not entirely') goes 'to the head' of LOIN.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang half-inch stands for pinch, which means to steal, a synonym of purloin.

clue.text: Mark's driven Peg around dip

indicators.note: around says the stake goes round the mark, enclosing it

parts.note: a picket is a pointed stake or peg driven into the ground
a pock is a mark on the skin; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark has hammered a tent peg round a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dip' is slang for a thief who steals from pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang a dip is a thief who lifts wallets from passers-by.

clue.text: After having to 16 amount, sons lying low (naughty laddies)

parts.note: the answer to 16 means steal, and nick is slang for steal

indicators.note: in a down clue lying low means placed at the bottom, so the letter for sons drops to the end

parts.note: a sum is an amount
S is the abbreviation for son or sons

explanation.surface: Mischievous lads lie low after stealing a sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying low' works because this is a down clue: the bottom of the light is its end. The parenthesis holds the definition, a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickum is a Scots word for a mischievous boy or rascal, so the plural means naughty lads.

clue.text: Three-in-one number encapsulating The King and I

indicators.note: encapsulating means holding inside, so the song wraps round the king and I

parts.note: a number is a song, a tune
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A medley from the musical The King and I combines three things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The King and I' looks like the musical's title; it gives R (rex) and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Triune describes being three in one, as in the Christian Trinity.

clue.text: The language repeatedly heard in wedding ceremony?

definitions.meaning: an artificial international tongue derived from Esperanto
the vow each partner says in a marriage service

explanation.surface: A wedding vow said again and again, mistaken for a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Ido is a constructed language, and 'I do' is the vow spoken by the bride and groom.

clue.text: Universal Pictures, not a Universal Church in retrospect

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking backwards, so the whole string reads from the end
not a says the letter A is dropped from the word for pictures

parts.note: the pictures is the cinema
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A film studio, Universal Pictures, is contrasted with a worldwide church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Universal Pictures' looks like the studio. CINEM + U + CE is then reversed by 'in retrospect'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecumenic means general or worldwide, especially across all Christian churches, which matches universal.

clue.text: Master taking on Chomsky — an old, personal confrontation

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
Noam Chomsky, the American linguist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A graduate takes on the linguist Chomsky in an old-fashioned one-to-one clash.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish phrase means hand to hand, a direct one-on-one showdown between two people.

clue.text: Take a little salt with …

definitions.meaning: to take something without permission, to steal it
a small amount held between finger and thumb

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction to add a little salt.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis leads into the next clue, which echoes the rhyme 'pinch, punch, first of the month'.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal is slang meaning of the word, and a tiny quantity of salt is a familiar recipe measure.

clue.text: … a spirited drink once weekly

definitions.meaning: a mixed party drink made with spirits, fruit juice and spices
the British satirical magazine, published every week until 2002

explanation.surface: Continuing 16: salt with a boozy drink, taken once a week.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch was a long-running British humorous magazine, printed weekly; 'once' says it no longer exists.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl drink mixed from spirits and fruit, and also the name of a former British weekly humour magazine.

clue.text: 17 and Viz: humour ultimately more like 17's conk

parts.note: the 17 answer is a blow, and a hook is a type of blow in boxing
viz and ie both mean 'that is', so viz gives IE

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word humour

explanation.surface: Mixing the magazines Punch and Viz, humour ends up more like a big nose.
explanation.walkthrough: Viz is a crude British comic magazine, but here 'viz' gives IE. Mr Punch, the puppet, has a hooked nose; 'conk' is British slang for nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Punch's nose is famously curved, so being more hooked is being more like it.

clue.text: Blow up a canal

parts.note: taken as written
per means a, as in so much a day
a cut is a man-made waterway or canal

explanation.surface: An instruction to blow up a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow up' looks like a phrasal verb, but 'Blow' is a noun, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An upward punch to the chin is a type of blow in boxing.

clue.text: Climbing mountain, main components of air have to part company

indicators.note: to part something is to split it, so the word to splits the mountain and the gases
in a down clue, climbing means the letters go upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
air is mostly nitrogen and oxygen, chemical symbols N and O
taken as written

explanation.surface: Climbers on a mountain, short of air, have to split up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part company' reads as a phrase, but 'part' says TO separates PLA (ALP reversed by 'Climbing') from the O and N of air; 'company' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a small body of soldiers, a military company in the loose sense of a group.

clue.text: Sacred mantra quelling Henry's resistance

indicators.note: quelling means keeping down or holding in, so the mantra encloses the letter

parts.note: om is the sacred syllable chanted in Hindu and Buddhist meditation
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: A chanted mantra calms Henry's urge to resist.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a man's name, but it is the unit of inductance, symbol H.
explanation.definitionFit: The ohm is the unit of electrical resistance.

clue.text: Tax firm going back over books to such an extent

indicators.note: going back says the tax and the firm are read in reverse order

parts.note: VAT is value added tax
CO is short for company, a firm
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A tax firm reviews accounts to an extreme degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'books' suggests accounts, but refers to a book size.
explanation.definitionFit: An octavo is a book size, made by folding sheets to give eight leaves, so books can be that size.

clue.text: A bit vulgar, going into auction without advance

indicators.note: going into means the vulgar word is put inside the auction word
without says the letter for advance is dropped from the auction

parts.note: a sale is an auction
A is an abbreviation for advance
naff is British slang for tasteless or vulgar

explanation.surface: A slightly crude person turns up at a sale without paying upfront.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit vulgar' reads as 'rather crude', but 'A bit' is the definition. NAFF is British slang for cheap and tasteless.
explanation.definitionFit: A snaffle is a simple jointed mouthpiece, a type of bit on a horse's bridle.

clue.text: Painting measuring up 22 x 0.25

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read upwards, so the words are reversed

parts.note: an oil is a painting in oils
of can mean measuring, as in a man of six feet

explanation.surface: A painting measured upwards comes to a quarter of a sum.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a sum: 22 is octavo, and a quarter of its eight leaves per sheet is two.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet folded once gives two leaves, a quarter of the eight leaves an octavo sheet gives.

clue.text: What may be cool and refreshing on back around lunchtime?

definitions.text: What may be cool and refreshing

indicators.note: back says the word for on is read backwards

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
at one o'clock, around lunchtime: AT and I for one

explanation.surface: A question about what is cool and reviving to eat around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, leg and on both name the same side of the field. I is the Roman numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian ice creams are cold and refreshing, so they may be described this way.

clue.text: Steal some time at work, during which ring public library

indicators.note: during which says the ring and the library sit inside the work period

parts.note: a shift is a period of work
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Skiving off work to ring the local library.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steal some time' looks like one phrase; 'Steal' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To take goods from a store without paying is stealing.

clue.text: … witness reporting second part of rescue

indicators.note: reporting means telling aloud, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: in the phrase air-sea rescue, the second part is sea

explanation.surface: A witness reports the second stage of a rescue operation.
explanation.walkthrough: This follows 4-down, which took the first part of air-sea rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness something is to observe it with your own eyes.

clue.text: Fairy wages?

definitions.meaning: the French word for a fairy

explanation.surface: A question about how much a fairy is paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Fée is French for fairy, and a charge or payment for work is a synonym of wages.

clue.text: Cruciverbalists' pasta that's filling — accompanying fine wallop!

indicators.note: accompanying says the fine letter sits next to the rest

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
crossword setters and solvers together say our

indicators.note: filling says the word for that goes into the pasta

parts.note: penne is tube-shaped pasta
yon is an old word for that; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: Crossword fans' pasta is filling, and comes with a fine punch.
explanation.walkthrough: A fourpenny one is old British slang for a punch or clout.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British terms for a hard blow.
